label: GO, late episode: after a reward when belief favours S2 (a2), scaled by trial cubed
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (1-belief) * (ep_trial/100)**3 ;; (phase == GO) * (1-belief) * (ep_trial/100)**3 ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (ep_trial/100)**3 ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (ep_trial/100)**3 ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (ep_trial/100)**3 ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * (ep_trial/100)**3 ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * (ep_trial/100)**3
explanation: Fires only at GO, and its magnitude grows steeply with episode trial (it is near zero before trial ~40). Effects beyond timing are multiplicative with that growth, so every term is scaled by (ep_trial/100)^3. The main driver is a reward on the last trial times the ideal observer belief that S2 is good (1-belief); weight +3.45, which outweighs the negative main effects of the reward and of 1-belief alone. In other words it fires when the agent has just been rewarded and the evidence points to a2. It is extra high after a2 S2 rewarded (+0.47) and lower after a2 S1 rewarded (rare transition, model-based switch to a1; -0.78) and after a1 S2 unrewarded (-0.76). When the trial before was also rewarded (a streak of a2 S2 rewards) it is lower (-0.81), so it is largest on the first reward after evidence turns toward S2 and then fades. It is zero at D1 and D2. Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.72 using observed quantities only, above the additive all ceiling of 0.31 because the terms interact with episode time. No future, hidden or model-output variables are used. The earlier firing label (GO, choosing a2 after reward, late) used the agent own choice; here belief stands in for the choice and loses little.

issues: Reproduced test R^2 beyond timing of 0.722 with the same weights. The core three terms (reward x (1-belief) x t^3 plus both main effects) score 0.653 on their own. The single interaction term scores 0.474. Without the t^3 scaling the same three terms score only 0.248, so the claim that the effect multiplies with episode time holds.

The explanation says the cost of dropping the model's policy is 'probably small' but never measured it. I checked with the observable upcoming choice (action==2, a future variable at GO) in place of belief: 0.601, below belief's 0.653. Adding action==2 to the belief terms gives 0.664, only +0.01. So the claim is supported, but the stated reasoning (comparing against the additive 'all' ceiling) was not a valid argument.
Calling 0.72 'above the additive all ceiling' compares unlike things. The ceiling is additive and has no time interaction, so it is not a real upper bound for these terms.

Small leftover systematic error at the very end of the episode. The timing baseline falls from decile 8 (0.649) to decile 9 (0.617), but t^3 keeps rising, so the worst dev misses are over-predictions at trials 96-99 (e.g. predicted 2.4 vs actual 0.83). A term for reward x (1-belief) x (ep_trial>=95) x t^3 gets weight -0.93 and lifts test R^2 to 0.742-0.750.

Some large under-predictions remain on the first reward of a run (actual about 2.6, predicted about 0.45, often at the window's first trial). Adding a belief_cover interaction or a rel==-3 term did not fix them (+0.000 / +0.002). The per-previous-trial mean errors are all small (|error| < 0.09), so these misses look scattered rather than a major systematic class.
The 'fades during a run of rewards' claim holds in general form: reward x (reward two trials back == 1) x t^3 has weight -0.40 to -0.84 depending on what else is in the model.
